Short title and commencement

ORDINANCE VII OF 1997
ORDINANCE VII OF 1997
EHTESAB (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance further to amend the
Ehtesab Ordinance, 1996
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part I, 17th January, 1997]
F.No.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 17‑1‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑
Whereas it is expedient further to
amend the Ehtesab Ordinance, 1996 (CXI of 1996), for the purposes hereinafter
appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore; in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
1. Short title and commencement.‑‑‑(1) This
Ordinance may be called the Ehtesab (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It shall come into force at once

2. Amendment of section 2, Ordinance
CXI of 1996.‑‑‑In
the Estesab Ordinance, 1996, (CXI of 1996), hereinafter referred to as the said
Ordinance, in section 2,‑‑
(i) the existing clause (a) shall be
re‑lettered as clause (aa) and before clause (aa) re‑lettered as
aforesaid the following new clause shall be inserted, namley:‑‑
"(a) 'accused' shall include a
person in respect of whom information under subsection (1) or subsection (2) of
section 16‑ shall be deemed to have been recorded;" and
(ii) for clause (d) the following
shall be substituted; namely:‑‑
"(d) 'Court' means a Bench of
not less than two nor more than three Judges of the High Court nominated by the
Chief Justice of the High Court.".

Now, therefore; in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
3. Amendment of section 3, Ordinance
CXI of 1996.‑‑In
the said Ordinance, in section 3,‑‑‑
(i) in subsection (3) after the word
"non‑bailable" the words "and, notwithstanding anything
contained in sections 497, 498 and 561 A or any other provision of the Code or
any other law for the time being in force, no Court other than the Court
defined in clause (d) of section 2 shall have jurisdiction to grant bail"
shall be added; and
(ii) after subsection (3) amended as
aforesaid the following new subsections shall be added, namely:‑‑‑
"(4) A holder of public office
accused of an offence under this Ordinance shall not be released on bail by the
Court if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty
of such an offence, nor shall an accused person be so released unless the Chief
Ehtesab Commissioner has been given notice of the bail application.
(5) Where a holder of public office
accused of an offence under this Ordinance is released on bail, the amount of
bail shall be fixed having regard to the gravity of the charge against such
person and, where the charge specifies any amount in respect of which the
offence is alleged to have been committed, shall not be less than twice the
said amount. "

Substitution of section 10, Ordinance CXI of 1996

following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑
Whereas it is expedient further to
amend the Ehtesab Ordinance, 1996 (CXI of 1996), for the purposes hereinafter
appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore; in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
4. Substitution of section 10,
Ordinance CXI of 1996.‑‑‑In the said Ordinance, for section 10 the following
shall be substituted, namely:‑‑‑
"10. Offences to be exclusively
triable by the Court.‑‑‑(1) Subject to the provisions of
subsection (2), and notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the
time being in force, an offence punishable under this Ordinance shall
exclusively be triable by a Bench of the High Court defined in clause (d) of
section 2 and the case shall be heard day to day and disposed of within sixty
days:
Provided that where the delay in the
trial is occasioned by any act or omission of the accused or any other person
acting on his behalf, the Court may direct that the accused shall cease to
perform the functions of his office either till the conclusion of the trial or
for such period as the Court may direct.
(2) Where more than one Benches have
been constituted in a High Court the cases referred to the High Court shall be
assigned to various Benches by the Chief Justice of the High Court."
Explanation. ‑‑‑In
this section, "High Court" means the High Court within the
jurisdiction of which the holder of public office is being proceeded against‑‑‑
(i) was elected as a member of Parliament
or a Provincial Assembly; or
(ii) resides, if such holder of
public office is a person specified in sub clause (i) or sub‑clause (iv)
of clause (f) of section 2.

6. Substitution of section 6,
Ordinance CXI of 1996.‑‑‑In the said Ordinance, for section 16, the
following shall be substituted, namely:‑‑‑
"16. Accused may be arrested in
certain cases, etc.‑‑‑(1) Where a reference is made to the
Chief Ehtesab Commissioner under clause (i) of subsection (2) of section 14,
such reference shall be deemed to be an information recorded under section 154
of the Code.
(2) Where the Chief Ehtesab
Commissioner initiates proceedings either on the receipt of a complaint or on
his own accord, and from the information received has reason to suspect the
commission of an offence under this Ordinance he may direct that such
information shall be treated as information recorded under section 154 of the
Code.
(3) A holder of public office
accused of an offence under this Ordinance shall not be arrested unless so
directed by the Chief Ehtesab Commissioner in writing. The direction given by
the Chief Ehtesab Commissioner shall contain the substance of the act of
corruption and corrupt practice alleged to have been committed by the accused
and a copy of such direction shall be forwarded to the Registrar of the Court
having jurisdiction to try the accused and another copy shall be given to the accused
on demand.
(4) Where a holder of public office
accused of any offence under this Ordinance is produced before a Judicial
Magistrate for police custody under section 167 of the Code, such Magistrate
may authorise the detention of such holder of public office in such custody for
a term not exceeding fourteen days in the whole".
